file_id: Sayan Mallick vs Unknown on 22 March, 2023

sentences.text: Sayan Mallick vs Unknown on 22 March, 2023

Author: Debangsu Basak Bench: Debangsu Basak 22.03.2023 Sl.9 Court No.29 C.R.M. (A) 1159 of 2023 (AD) In Re: - An application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of (Allowed) the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with Haringhta Police Station Case No.310 of 2022 dated 25.08.2022 under Sections 341/323/325/354/376/511/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
And In the matter of: Sayan Mallick ....petitioner.
Ms. Minoti Gomes Mr. Partha Sarathi Das Ms. Shanta Sarkar ... for the petitioner.
Mr. Gautam Banerjee ...for the State.
There is a previous police complaint.
Apparently, there was a free fight between the parties.
Injuries do not suggest that any person suffered grievous hurt.
In such circumstances, we grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest, the petitioner shall be released on bail upon furnishing a Bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand Only), with two sureties of like amount each, to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and on condition that the petitioner will report before the Investigating Officer once a month till the conclusion of the investigation and on condition that the petitioner shall appear on every date before the jurisdictional Court on and from the date fixed for appearance of the accused and in default the jurisdictional Court will pass appropriate order to secure the presence of the petitioner in Court including cancelling the anticipatory bail granted without further reference to this Court.
Accordingly, the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner is allowed.
C.R.M. (A) 1159 of 2023 is, thus, disposed of.

(Debangsu Basak, J.) (Md. Shabbar Rashidi, J.)
